_comment: Papers managed on Zenodo. concept: the concept record id (its DOI resolves to the latest version). files: Zenodo file name -> repository path. A new version copies the latest version's metadata (title, description, keywords, license, resource type) and sets the fields under 'version'. Use scripts/zenodo.py. A paper without 'concept' is created as a new record from 'new'; after it is published, record its concept id here. 'build' names a LaTeX directory whose main.tex is compiled with tectonic and packed into source.tar.gz before upload. meta (metadata only, no new version): creators, keywords_core plus each paper's keywords, the references parsed from references_from, and related identifiers: the repo and site, and 'cites' / 'isCitedBy' links between papers by concept DOI.

new.title: The Categorical Structure of Federated Convergence: Limits, Sheaves, and Minimal Coordination
new.description:
Normalization confluence gives coordination-free convergence within a single registry, and its federated extension gives a unique federated repair normal form across a network of registries connected by morphisms, in two decidable regimes: acyclic networks, and monotone repair on cycles. Convergence of event order is a further condition: the cross-registry conditions C1 and C2 on acyclic networks (events firing at federally valid states), and the global condition GC on cycles. This paper gives the structure underneath the repair layer and, with it, an answer to a sharper question: when must a federation coordinate at all, and how little coordination suffices?

We show that a federation's consistent states are a finite limit and, under an explicit shared-component stability hypothesis, its federated normalizer is the idempotent retraction onto that limit, independent of the topological order, so compositionality (a verified sub-federation collapses to an effective registry) follows from one structural fact rather than a per-topology argument. On the site whose open sets are sub-federations, consistent states glue exactly when every constraint lies inside one member of the cover, given the source-determinacy hypothesis the federation already certifies, and the certificates of sub-federations closed under sources glue under shared-component stability. The obstruction to a global consistent state is cohomological in the invertible fragment: H^0 is the consistent states and H^1 is the holonomy of the morphism cycles. Acyclicity and monotone repair are two sufficient routes to a non-empty H^0, though not the only ones. Around a cycle, a section exists iff the loop composite over the shared subspace has a fixed point; the reference engine's cycle diagnostic tests one seed, which proves existence when it settles and, for a free (regular) action, refutes it when it orbits. Finally, in the invertible fragment with the regular action and a designated authority root, coordinating exactly the unbalanced non-tree edges of a spanning tree is sound, with a unique normal form for each authority value, and no smaller subset of those edges suffices, localizing the global coordination criterion of CALM and invariant confluence into a mixed-consistency partition. The exact minimum coordination is the group feedback edge set number of the labeled nerve: NP-hard even in the abelian case, fixed-parameter tractable in the size of the coordinated core, and never below the minimum for any homomorphic image of the transition group. The structural and cohomological results, the registry-level gluing, the mathematics of the diagnostic, the coordination plan and the reduction from Max-Cut are mechanized axiom-free in Coq/Rocq, together with a counterexample for every statement of version 1 that this version corrects; the variable-level sheaf reading and the cited complexity results are not mechanized.

new.title: Normalization confluence: an exact, mechanized theory of when repair can replace commutativity
new.description: Replicas that apply the same events in different orders, and repair their business invariants after each event, need not end in the same state. We give an exact theory of when they do: raw states may differ, but the result after repair must agree. We state a condition at each of three scales: state descent, necessary at a single event; history descent over finite histories, which with state descent and terminating repair is necessary and sufficient for a single registry; and canonical recurrence, necessary and sufficient for infinite runs on finite state spaces. We prove the hierarchy between them and show that CRDTs are the case where repair does nothing: repair enlarges which operations can be used, while every convergent repaired system is a CRDT on its repaired steps. A three-layer framework for executions, consistent states and long-run behavior, with proved interfaces, organizes these conditions across a map of regimes that has, in every regime, an exact condition, a hardness result or a listed open problem. We test the framework where it could fail: with its files frozen it recovers Dijkstra's self-stabilization and invariant confluence, and two predictions committed before their tests were confirmed, one about stable matching markets and one about replication in CouchDB and PouchDB. All 4,766 gated results are mechanized in Coq with no axioms.
